title: Valgus Motion
note: Generated by tools/figures.py --extract from the page itself. Edit the verification and source fields; everything else is rewritten on the next extraction. A figure the reviewer corrects or deletes is marked REMOVED rather than removed from this file.

figures.claim: Conventional teaching gives physiological valgus alignment as about 5 to 7 degrees, with women on average slightly higher than men.
Testing at 20 to 30 degrees of flexion isolates the collateral ligament, because the secondary restraints contribute less there.
The superficial collateral carries the large majority of valgus restraint at 25 degrees of flexion, with the posteromedial corner taking an increasing share towards extension.
Conventional teaching grades medial injury by the opening at 30 degrees: a few millimetres for grade one and two, and a complete loss of endpoint for grade three.
Valgus stress testing at 0 and 30 degrees, graded by opening and endpoint.
